questions.topic: Trainee employment limit: minimum experience exception
questions.trigger: A 19-year-old holds a valid Massachusetts pharmacy technician trainee license. Thirteen months after starting employment, the trainee has accumulated 420 hours. No Board extension has been granted. Which actions are permissible under the trainee rules?
questions.legal_decision: Allow continued directly supervised trainee work until the minimum-experience exception ceases, but do not allow telephone prescriptions.
questions.critical_exception: The trainee has not yet completed 500 hours; active trainee license and supervision still required.
questions.counterfactual_flip: At 500 hours, the one-year limit would bar further trainee work absent another exception.
questions.stem: A 19-year-old holds a valid Massachusetts pharmacy technician trainee license. Thirteen months after starting employment, the trainee has accumulated 420 hours. No Board extension has been granted. Which actions are permissible under the trainee rules? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Permit continued trainee work under direct pharmacist supervision.
choices.why: Correct. The minimum-experience exception permits continuing while fewer than 500 hours have been completed.

choices.text: Require immediate dismissal solely because one year has passed.
choices.why: Incorrect. The elapsed-year limit has an express exception for this trainee.

choices.text: Count the trainee as a certified technician in the supervision ratio.
choices.why: Incorrect. Time employed does not confer certification or change the personnel category.

choices.text: Keep telephone prescription intake outside the trainee's duties.
choices.why: Correct. The restriction on receiving prescriptions by telephone remains applicable.

choices.text: Treat the trainee as independently licensed once 500 hours are reached.
choices.why: Incorrect. Meeting the experience threshold does not itself confer a technician license.

questions.topic: Maximum continuing education credit per calendar day
questions.trigger: A pharmacist attends a ten-contact-hour accredited conference on a single calendar day. All subjects are otherwise acceptable for Massachusetts renewal. What is the maximum credit the pharmacist may earn for that day?
questions.legal_decision: Count at most eight contact hours for the calendar day.
questions.critical_exception: Assume no Board-granted individual exception; the limitation applies to credits earned per day.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the conference's eligible hours were completed across two days with no more than eight on either day, all ten could count.
questions.stem: A pharmacist attends a ten-contact-hour accredited conference on a single calendar day. All subjects are otherwise acceptable for Massachusetts renewal. What is the maximum credit the pharmacist may earn for that day?

choices.text: Ten, because the provider accredited all ten hours.
choices.why: Incorrect. Accreditation does not eliminate the Massachusetts daily ceiling.

choices.text: Five, because conference credit is limited like mediated instruction.
choices.why: Incorrect. The separate annual home-study limitation does not establish a five-hour daily cap.

choices.text: Eight contact hours.
choices.why: Correct. The regulation limits the amount earned on one calendar day to eight hours.

choices.text: Seven, unless the conference contains two hours of pharmacy law.
choices.why: Incorrect. The pharmacy-law subject requirement does not alter the daily cap.

choices.text: Ten, provided the extra two are carried into the next calendar year.
choices.why: Incorrect. The daily cap cannot be bypassed by carrying credit into another year.

questions.topic: CE renewal petition for disability-related mediated instruction
questions.trigger: Because of a physical disability, a pharmacist cannot comply with the annual limit on home-study continuing education. The pharmacist seeks renewal and has completed twenty hours of otherwise acceptable mediated instruction. Which statements describe the appropriate Massachusetts process?
questions.legal_decision: Submit a detailed statement under penalties of perjury; await the Board's renewal determination.
questions.critical_exception: The Board decides whether to grant renewal under the extenuating-circumstances provision.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the pharmacist instead satisfies the ordinary CE limits, this exception petition is unnecessary.
questions.stem: Because of a physical disability, a pharmacist cannot comply with the annual limit on home-study continuing education. The pharmacist seeks renewal and has completed twenty hours of otherwise acceptable mediated instruction. Which statements describe the appropriate Massachusetts process? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: The pharmacist may self-approve the exception on the renewal application.
choices.why: Incorrect. A disability does not create a self-executing waiver.

choices.text: Provide a specific written explanation under the penalties of perjury.
choices.why: Correct. The regulation requires a detailed sworn statement explaining the circumstances.

choices.text: The CE provider may authorize unlimited mediated hours on behalf of the Board.
choices.why: Incorrect. An education provider cannot make the Board's renewal decision.

choices.text: The pharmacist must abandon the renewal application without requesting consideration.
choices.why: Incorrect. The regulation expressly provides a route for extenuating circumstances.

choices.text: The Board decides whether renewal will be granted.
choices.why: Correct. The Board, rather than the applicant, makes the determination and communicates its reasons.

questions.topic: Daily internship credit versus time worked
questions.trigger: An intern's log contains a 13-hour entry for one calendar day. Assume all work was supervised and eligible, and no other practice-hours issue is being evaluated. How many internship credit hours can be awarded for that day?
questions.legal_decision: Limit the internship credit entry to 12 hours.
questions.critical_exception: The question concerns credit only, not whether a particular shift schedule is permitted.
questions.counterfactual_flip: For 11 otherwise eligible hours on a single day, 11 may be credited.
questions.stem: An intern's log contains a 13-hour entry for one calendar day. Assume all work was supervised and eligible, and no other practice-hours issue is being evaluated. How many internship credit hours can be awarded for that day?

choices.text: Thirteen, because every supervised hour is automatically creditable.
choices.why: Incorrect. Direct supervision does not eliminate the daily credit maximum.

choices.text: Twelve hours.
choices.why: Correct. The maximum credit for a calendar day is twelve.

choices.text: Eight, because CE and internship credit have the same daily limit.
choices.why: Incorrect. The eight-hour ceiling pertains to pharmacist CE, not internship credit.

choices.text: Zero, because exceeding the maximum invalidates the entire day.
choices.why: Incorrect. The rule limits credited hours; it does not say all credit for the day is forfeited.

choices.text: Thirteen if the excess is entered on the next day's log.
choices.why: Incorrect. The limit applies to when experience actually occurs, not when it is entered.

questions.topic: Certified technician's certification lapse with active state license
questions.trigger: An employee's national certification lapses, but the employee retains an active Massachusetts pharmacy technician license. Which changes must the manager make until the certification is restored?
questions.legal_decision: Restrict scope to ordinary technician duties, change title and count as an ordinary technician.
questions.critical_exception: The state technician license remains active.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If state licensure also lapses, technician practice itself must stop.
questions.stem: An employee's national certification lapses, but the employee retains an active Massachusetts pharmacy technician license. Which changes must the manager make until the certification is restored? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Restrict the employee to ordinary pharmacy technician duties.
choices.why: Correct. The certification lapse removes certified-technician-specific scope.

choices.text: Terminate all technician duties even though the state license is active.
choices.why: Incorrect. The regulation permits ordinary technician duties during a certification lapse.

choices.text: Change the employee's displayed title to pharmacy technician.
choices.why: Correct. The certified designation is no longer appropriate.

choices.text: Continue counting the employee as certified until the next payroll period.
choices.why: Incorrect. Supervision ratios depend on current status, not payroll timing.

choices.text: Count the employee in the ordinary technician category for ratios.
choices.why: Correct. The lapse changes the category used in calculating supervision ratios.

questions.topic: Nonsterile compounding designated person
questions.trigger: A Massachusetts pharmacy performs simple nonsterile compounding. The manager proposes naming an experienced, certified technician as the sole USP <795> designated person because the manager works at another site on some days. Under Board Policy 2023-07, who may fulfill the designated-person requirement?
questions.legal_decision: Use the manager of record or an on-site licensed pharmacist, not technician certification alone.
questions.critical_exception: This is the Massachusetts Board's nonsterile compounding policy, not the separate hazardous-drug designated-person framework.
questions.counterfactual_flip: Replacing the technician with an on-site licensed pharmacist satisfies the stated personnel condition.
questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy performs simple nonsterile compounding. The manager proposes naming an experienced, certified technician as the sole USP <795> designated person because the manager works at another site on some days. Under Board Policy 2023-07, who may fulfill the designated-person requirement?

choices.text: Any nationally certified pharmacy technician with five years of compounding experience.
choices.why: Incorrect. Experience and national technician certification do not match the Board's stated designated-person roles.

choices.text: A pharmacist employed by another pharmacy who only reviews the monthly logs remotely.
choices.why: Incorrect. The policy specifies the pharmacy's manager of record or an on-site licensed pharmacist.

choices.text: Any technician whose work is checked by a pharmacist at the end of each shift.
choices.why: Incorrect. Supervision of the technician's work is not a substitute for the designated-person role.

choices.text: The manager of record or an on-site licensed pharmacist.
choices.why: Correct. These are the roles identified by the Board for the USP <795> designated person.

choices.text: Only an independently employed consultant pharmacist who is not the manager of record.
choices.why: Incorrect. The manager of record is expressly eligible.

questions.topic: Ordinary technician receiving modified refill authorization
questions.trigger: With the pharmacist's approval, a noncertified Massachusetts pharmacy technician requests renewal of a Schedule VI prescription. The prescriber's office authorizes renewal but changes the tablet strength. What should the technician do?
questions.legal_decision: Refer the changed prescription information to appropriately authorized personnel; ordinary technician refill authority covers unchanged information.
questions.critical_exception: No emergency or other special authority is assumed.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the authorized refill had no changes from the previous prescription, the ordinary technician could accept it with approval.
questions.stem: With the pharmacist's approval, a noncertified Massachusetts pharmacy technician requests renewal of a Schedule VI prescription. The prescriber's office authorizes renewal but changes the tablet strength. What should the technician do?

choices.text: Refer the changed-strength order to the pharmacist.
choices.why: Correct. Ordinary technician authority to receive a refill authorization is conditioned on unchanged prescription information.

choices.text: Accept the new strength because the prescriber called it a renewal.
choices.why: Incorrect. The change in strength, not the office's terminology, controls the technician's scope.

choices.text: Enter the old strength and leave a note about the new one for later.
choices.why: Incorrect. This would misrepresent the prescriber's order and create a dispensing risk.

choices.text: Accept the changed strength because Schedule VI drugs are not federally controlled.
choices.why: Incorrect. Massachusetts personnel restrictions still apply to Schedule VI prescriptions.

choices.text: Accept the change as long as the pharmacist performs final validation later.
choices.why: Incorrect. Final validation does not enlarge the technician's authority to receive changed information.

questions.topic: Expired researcher registration at participating retail pharmacy
questions.trigger: A retail pharmacy participating in a Massachusetts research drug study has a patient-specific prescription under an approved protocol. Its pharmacy license remains active, but the researcher's MCSR specifying this site has expired. Which actions comply with Board policy?
questions.legal_decision: Pause research participation until renewal of the researcher MCSR; verify the site remains included.
questions.critical_exception: The researcher-specific MCSR is separate from the pharmacy's ordinary license.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the researcher MCSR is renewed and still lists the site, the registration barrier is resolved.
questions.stem: A retail pharmacy participating in a Massachusetts research drug study has a patient-specific prescription under an approved protocol. Its pharmacy license remains active, but the researcher's MCSR specifying this site has expired. Which actions comply with Board policy? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Continue filling study prescriptions under the pharmacy's own active registration.
choices.why: Incorrect. The policy specifically requires an active researcher MCSR for the participating site.

choices.text: Continue participation if the investigator sends a written assurance that renewal is pending.
choices.why: Incorrect. A pending renewal does not make the expired registration effective.

choices.text: Suspend participation in the study until the researcher MCSR is renewed.
choices.why: Correct. The policy bars continued participation under an expired researcher registration.

choices.text: Confirm the participating pharmacy address is specified on the renewed researcher MCSR.
choices.why: Correct. Participation is site-specific and requires inclusion in the approved researcher registration.

choices.text: Dispense study medication on the assumption that patient-specific orders replace the registration requirement.
choices.why: Incorrect. A valid prescription is necessary but does not replace the separate registration.

questions.topic: Bulk API source and identity before preparation
questions.trigger: A pharmacy receives an active ingredient powder from a supplier. The invoice does not establish that the supplying facility is FDA-registered or whether the powder is a pure ingredient or a diluted trituration. Which steps are appropriate before using the material in a nonsterile preparation?
questions.legal_decision: Verify both registered facility status and concentration/identity before calculating and compounding.
questions.critical_exception: The case involves API powder rather than a conventionally manufactured finished product.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If both the registered source and verified powder concentration are established, these two barriers are removed.
questions.stem: A pharmacy receives an active ingredient powder from a supplier. The invoice does not establish that the supplying facility is FDA-registered or whether the powder is a pure ingredient or a diluted trituration. Which steps are appropriate before using the material in a nonsterile preparation? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Verify that the API came from an FDA-registered facility.
choices.why: Correct. The policy specifies the source registration condition.

choices.text: Determine whether the powder is pure or diluted before calculating quantities.
choices.why: Correct. A trituration can contain less active ingredient per gram; assuming purity can cause a dosing error.

choices.text: Use the labeled gross powder weight as the active ingredient amount without verification.
choices.why: Incorrect. The gross mass may include diluent and cannot establish active concentration.

choices.text: Treat the supplier's business registration with the state as sufficient evidence of FDA registration.
choices.why: Incorrect. State business status alone does not establish the federal facility registration required by the policy.

choices.text: Proceed based on the prescriber's willingness to accept the uncertainty.
choices.why: Incorrect. Prescriber agreement does not remove the pharmacy's compounding quality duties.

questions.topic: One-log documentation option for premeasured kits
questions.trigger: A pharmacy uses premeasured nonsterile compounding kits. The manager maintains a single readily retrievable log with all information specified in Board Policy 2023-07, including component traceability, relevant quantities, beyond-use date and preparer identification. Which documentation arrangement is permissible?
questions.legal_decision: The complete kit compounding record may also serve as the master formulation record.
questions.critical_exception: Special documentation option applies to premeasured kits and flavoring of conventional nonsterile products, not all compounds.
questions.counterfactual_flip: For an ordinary bulk-ingredient preparation outside the specified categories, the special combined-log option does not apply.
questions.stem: A pharmacy uses premeasured nonsterile compounding kits. The manager maintains a single readily retrievable log with all information specified in Board Policy 2023-07, including component traceability, relevant quantities, beyond-use date and preparer identification. Which documentation arrangement is permissible?

choices.text: Eliminate the log because all ingredients were premeasured by the kit manufacturer.
choices.why: Incorrect. Using a kit is still compounding and requires documentation.

choices.text: Keep only the kit invoice, patient name and dispensing date.
choices.why: Incorrect. An invoice and dispensing information do not contain all required compounding data.

choices.text: Keep a formulation sheet only, without any record of the actual preparation.
choices.why: Incorrect. Preparation-specific documentation is still required.

choices.text: Maintain a separate master formulation record in every case, even when the policy's complete kit log is used.
choices.why: Incorrect. The Board provides a limited combined-record option for these preparations.

choices.text: Use the complete log as both required records.
choices.why: Correct. The specific kit exception allows the compounding record to serve as the master formulation record.

questions.topic: Flavor additive compatibility and concentration
questions.trigger: A parent requests flavoring for a Schedule VI oral solution. The pharmacy has a flavoring policy but no evidence that the proposed additive preserves stability and acceptable final concentration. Which response is appropriate?
questions.legal_decision: Do not add the flavor until stability and concentration compatibility are established; patient request can support adding flavor without a new prescriber request.
questions.critical_exception: Schedule VI flavoring upon patient or agent request is permitted; quality requirements remain.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If reliable relevant evidence establishes compatibility and all other requirements are satisfied, the pharmacy can proceed.
questions.stem: A parent requests flavoring for a Schedule VI oral solution. The pharmacy has a flavoring policy but no evidence that the proposed additive preserves stability and acceptable final concentration. Which response is appropriate? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Add any flavoring volume the parent selects because the drug is Schedule VI.
choices.why: Incorrect. Patient preference does not replace stability and concentration controls.

choices.text: Verify that adding the flavor will not compromise stability or concentration within applicable standards.
choices.why: Correct. The policy requires evidence that flavoring does not adversely affect the product.

choices.text: Refuse all patient-requested flavoring unless the prescriber writes a completely new prescription.
choices.why: Incorrect. The policy allows Schedule VI flavoring at patient or agent request under its conditions.

choices.text: Use suitable scientific data to support the compatibility determination.
choices.why: Correct. The Board permits relevant published or unpublished scientific data for this purpose.

choices.text: Assume flavoring is exempt from compounding requirements because the starting product is commercially manufactured.
choices.why: Incorrect. Adding flavor is considered compounding under the Board policy.

questions.topic: Veterinary emergency kit annual written agreement
questions.trigger: A pharmacy supplies a veterinary emergency kit under Joint Policy 2019-06. The veterinarian's MCSR remains active and the kit contains only eligible compounded Schedule VI medicines. The formulary agreement has not been reviewed or renewed in 18 months. Which action is needed before continuing the arrangement?
questions.legal_decision: Review and renew the written formulary agreement before continuing kit supply.
questions.critical_exception: All other veterinary kit conditions are assumed satisfied.
questions.counterfactual_flip: An agreement reviewed and renewed within the past year would remove this deficiency.
questions.stem: A pharmacy supplies a veterinary emergency kit under Joint Policy 2019-06. The veterinarian's MCSR remains active and the kit contains only eligible compounded Schedule VI medicines. The formulary agreement has not been reviewed or renewed in 18 months. Which action is needed before continuing the arrangement?

choices.text: Continue under the old agreement because the MCSR has not expired.
choices.why: Incorrect. Current veterinarian registration does not satisfy the separate agreement requirement.

choices.text: Allow the veterinarian to substitute medicines in the kit without notifying the pharmacy.
choices.why: Incorrect. The written agreement must identify the specific kit formulary.

choices.text: Review and renew the written formulary agreement.
choices.why: Correct. The policy requires review and renewal at least annually.

choices.text: Transfer the kit to the veterinarian as ordinary unrestricted office stock.
choices.why: Incorrect. Under this arrangement the medicines remain the pharmacy's responsibility and inventory until patient-specific prescriptions are provided.

choices.text: Replace the agreement with a verbal approval from the veterinarian.
choices.why: Incorrect. The agreement must be written and specify the formulary.

questions.topic: HIPAA notice revision and acknowledgement
questions.trigger: A HIPAA-covered pharmacy previously gave an established patient its notice of privacy practices and obtained an acknowledgement. The pharmacy revises the notice. Assume no new first-service encounter and no other rule requiring another signature. Which steps are appropriate?
questions.legal_decision: Make the revised notice available as required; do not require a new acknowledgement solely because it was revised.
questions.critical_exception: A revision alone does not require a repeated acknowledgement.
questions.counterfactual_flip: A new patient at first service triggers the applicable initial notice and good-faith acknowledgement requirement, absent an emergency.
questions.stem: A HIPAA-covered pharmacy previously gave an established patient its notice of privacy practices and obtained an acknowledgement. The pharmacy revises the notice. Assume no new first-service encounter and no other rule requiring another signature. Which steps are appropriate? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Make the revised notice available as required by the Privacy Rule.
choices.why: Correct. The pharmacy must comply with the revised-notice distribution and availability requirements.

choices.text: Refuse refills until every established patient signs another acknowledgement.
choices.why: Incorrect. A revised notice alone does not trigger a new acknowledgement requirement.

choices.text: Treat the old acknowledgement as consent to disclose information for any purpose newly described in the notice.
choices.why: Incorrect. Acknowledgement of receipt is not a blanket HIPAA authorization.

choices.text: Require a new acknowledgement at every refill whenever a notice is revised.
choices.why: Incorrect. HHS distinguishes notice availability from a new acknowledgement on revision.

choices.text: Do not demand a repeat acknowledgement solely because the notice changed.
choices.why: Correct. HHS confirms that a new acknowledgement is not required on revision alone.

questions.citation: 45 CFR 164.520(c)(2); HHS FAQ on revised notices

questions.topic: Incidental disclosure at pharmacy pickup
questions.trigger: In a busy HIPAA-covered pharmacy, patients wait for prescriptions. A staff member proposes loudly calling each patient's full name, drug and diagnosis to speed pickup. Which approaches are consistent with reasonable privacy safeguards?
questions.legal_decision: Use limited name calls when reasonable; avoid unnecessarily announcing the drug and diagnosis; protect information during counseling.
questions.critical_exception: Incidental disclosure is permissible only when the underlying use is permitted and safeguards are reasonable.
questions.counterfactual_flip: A permitted private discussion with the patient about the drug may disclose details that should not be broadcast to the waiting area.
questions.stem: In a busy HIPAA-covered pharmacy, patients wait for prescriptions. A staff member proposes loudly calling each patient's full name, drug and diagnosis to speed pickup. Which approaches are consistent with reasonable privacy safeguards? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Announce the diagnosis with the patient's name because the pharmacy is providing treatment.
choices.why: Incorrect. A permissible treatment use does not justify unnecessary public disclosure of sensitive details.

choices.text: Use a limited name call when reasonably necessary to identify the waiting patient.
choices.why: Correct. HHS permits limited incidental disclosures with appropriate safeguards.

choices.text: Avoid announcing medication and diagnosis details to the entire waiting area.
choices.why: Correct. Reasonable safeguards reduce unnecessary disclosures of protected health information.

choices.text: Prohibit all verbal identification even if it is reasonably limited and necessary.
choices.why: Incorrect. HIPAA does not categorically prohibit incidental disclosures that satisfy its conditions.

choices.text: Move detailed counseling to a setting that protects privacy as reasonably practicable.
choices.why: Correct. Reasonable safeguards apply to conversations involving sensitive information.

questions.citation: 45 CFR 164.502(a)(1)(iii), 164.530(c); HHS incidental uses and disclosures guidance

questions.topic: Massachusetts narcotic pamphlet exceptions
questions.trigger: A Massachusetts community pharmacy dispenses qualifying Schedule II or III narcotic prescriptions to several patients. Which patients fall within express exceptions to the state's consumer narcotics-pamphlet distribution requirement? Assume other counseling and legal duties remain applicable.
questions.legal_decision: Apply the pamphlet-specific exceptions for outpatient palliative care, LTCF residency, and treatment of SUD or opioid dependence.
questions.critical_exception: The exceptions concern this pamphlet only, not all counseling or other dispensing duties.
questions.counterfactual_flip: A routine postoperative outpatient narcotic prescription outside the exceptions triggers the pamphlet requirement.
questions.stem: A Massachusetts community pharmacy dispenses qualifying Schedule II or III narcotic prescriptions to several patients. Which patients fall within express exceptions to the state's consumer narcotics-pamphlet distribution requirement? Assume other counseling and legal duties remain applicable. SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: A patient receiving qualifying outpatient palliative care under c. 111, § 227.
choices.why: Correct. The statute expressly lists this outpatient palliative care exception.

choices.text: A routine postoperative patient receiving a second prescription for a narcotic.
choices.why: Incorrect. A prior dispensing does not itself establish one of the listed exceptions.

choices.text: A resident of a long-term care facility.
choices.why: Correct. LTCF residence is an express exception to the pamphlet requirement.

choices.text: A patient receiving the prescribed narcotic to treat opioid dependence.
choices.why: Correct. Use to treat substance use disorder or opioid dependence is expressly excepted.

choices.text: A patient who pays cash and has no insurance claim.
choices.why: Incorrect. Payment method does not determine the pamphlet exception.

questions.topic: Research study site withdrawal notification
questions.trigger: A participating pharmacy elects to stop providing study medicines. The investigator will continue the study at other sites, and the pharmacy retains its usual license. What must this pharmacy do regarding the Board and its study approval records?
questions.legal_decision: Notify the Board of withdrawal and keep participation approval or waiver records available for inspection.
questions.critical_exception: The pharmacy is ending its own participation even though the overall study continues.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the pharmacy continues participating in the active study, this withdrawal notification trigger has not occurred.
questions.stem: A participating pharmacy elects to stop providing study medicines. The investigator will continue the study at other sites, and the pharmacy retains its usual license. What must this pharmacy do regarding the Board and its study approval records? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Wait until the entire research study terminates before informing the Board.
choices.why: Incorrect. The policy also requires notice when an individual pharmacy ceases participation.

choices.text: Discard the study approval documentation as soon as the last prescription is dispensed.
choices.why: Incorrect. The pharmacy must retain participation approval and waiver documents for Board inspection.

choices.text: Notify the Board that this pharmacy will no longer participate.
choices.why: Correct. Withdrawal of the site is an independent notification trigger.

choices.text: Cancel the pharmacy's regular pharmacy license because study participation ended.
choices.why: Incorrect. Termination of a research arrangement does not itself require closing the retail pharmacy.

choices.text: Keep participation approval and waiver records available for Board inspection.
choices.why: Correct. The policy requires maintenance and availability of these documents.

questions.topic: Automated compounding device validation before patient use
questions.trigger: A 503A pharmacy plans to prepare patient-specific nonsterile medications using a new automated compounding device. The sales representative claims the device eliminates the need to confirm validation and ingredient compatibility. Which checks does the Massachusetts Board's November 2025 memorandum require?
questions.legal_decision: Verify device regulatory status or manufacturer validation documentation, ingredient compatibility, cleanability and continued pharmacy responsibility.
questions.critical_exception: Use is allowed only while relevant USP and other state and federal requirements are satisfied.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If documentary validation/status and compatibility and cleaning checks are completed, these identified readiness barriers are removed.
questions.stem: A 503A pharmacy plans to prepare patient-specific nonsterile medications using a new automated compounding device. The sales representative claims the device eliminates the need to confirm validation and ingredient compatibility. Which checks does the Massachusetts Board's November 2025 memorandum require? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Determine whether the device has or requires FDA approval, or establish manufacturer validation through documentation as applicable.
choices.why: Correct. The Board requires a regulatory-status or documented-validation assessment.

choices.text: Confirm compatibility of the relevant active ingredients with the device.
choices.why: Correct. Device suitability must be evaluated for the ingredients used.

choices.text: Transfer responsibility for preparation accuracy entirely to the equipment manufacturer.
choices.why: Incorrect. The pharmacy remains responsible regardless of the device used.

choices.text: Confirm that the device is readily cleanable to minimize cross-contamination.
choices.why: Correct. Cleanability is one of the Board's specified checks.

choices.text: Continue applying USP <800> if the device is used for hazardous-drug compounding.
choices.why: Correct. Automation does not remove hazardous-drug containment and handling obligations.

questions.citation: Massachusetts Board memorandum, Automated Non-Sterile Compounding Devices, Nov. 6, 2025, items 1-3

questions.topic: Worksite delivery with undelivered prescriptions
questions.trigger: A pharmacy collects eligible prescriptions in person at an employer's worksite. At delivery, two patients are absent and the receptionist is not their authorized agent. Which actions comply with the Massachusetts worksite prescription rules?
questions.legal_decision: Deliver directly to the patient or agent; return undelivered items to the pharmacy.
questions.critical_exception: Specific worksite collection/delivery arrangement; receptionist is not a patient's agent.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the receptionist is genuinely authorized as the patient's agent, direct delivery to that agent may be permissible.
questions.stem: A pharmacy collects eligible prescriptions in person at an employer's worksite. At delivery, two patients are absent and the receptionist is not their authorized agent. Which actions comply with the Massachusetts worksite prescription rules? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Leave the absent patients' prescriptions at reception because the building is access-controlled.
choices.why: Incorrect. Undelivered prescriptions cannot be left or stored at the delivery site.

choices.text: Return prescriptions that cannot be delivered directly to the pharmacy.
choices.why: Correct. The worksite rule expressly requires return of undelivered medicines.

choices.text: Ask the employer to take custody without confirming any patient authorization.
choices.why: Incorrect. Employment at the site does not make the employer a patient's authorized agent.

choices.text: Deliver prescriptions directly to the patient or the patient's authorized agent.
choices.why: Correct. Direct delivery to the patient or agent is required under this arrangement.

choices.text: Shift responsibility for the delivery employee's conduct to the employer.
choices.why: Incorrect. The pharmacist and pharmacy retain responsibility for the conduct of their employee or authorized agent.

questions.topic: Accessible prescription directions upon patient request
questions.trigger: A visually impaired patient asks a Massachusetts pharmacist for larger printed directions on a prescription container. The standard label printer produces 14 characters per inch. Which label change meets the specific Massachusetts statutory print-size requirement?
questions.legal_decision: Print directions with no more than ten characters per inch.
questions.critical_exception: The triggering fact is a request from a visually impaired or qualifying elderly person.
questions.counterfactual_flip: Without such a request, this specific statutory print-size mandate is not triggered; other accessibility duties may still apply.
questions.stem: A visually impaired patient asks a Massachusetts pharmacist for larger printed directions on a prescription container. The standard label printer produces 14 characters per inch. Which label change meets the specific Massachusetts statutory print-size requirement?

choices.text: Use a label with at least 14 characters per inch and supply a verbal explanation.
choices.why: Incorrect. Verbal counseling does not satisfy the requested statutory print requirement.

choices.text: Print at exactly ten points, regardless of the number of characters per inch.
choices.why: Incorrect. The statute expresses its requirement in characters per inch, not point size.

choices.text: Print only the drug name in large type and leave the directions unchanged.
choices.why: Incorrect. The statute specifically addresses the directions on the label.

choices.text: Print the directions at no more than ten characters per inch.
choices.why: Correct. This meets the statutory character-density limit.

choices.text: Wait for the prescriber to order a large-print label.
choices.why: Incorrect. The qualifying patient's request triggers this requirement without a separate prescriber order.

questions.topic: Schedule VI oral order and follow-up document
questions.trigger: A Massachusetts practitioner validly issues an oral Schedule VI prescription under an applicable electronic-prescribing exception. The pharmacist receives all required information. Which statements apply to documentation of this oral order?
questions.legal_decision: Reduce the oral prescription to a complete written record; the §20(c) two-day follow-up requirement does not apply to Schedule VI.
questions.critical_exception: The oral order is otherwise authorized and lawful; the exception is limited to §20(c).
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the prescription instead concerns a Schedule III controlled substance, the applicable §20(c) follow-up requirement must be considered.
questions.stem: A Massachusetts practitioner validly issues an oral Schedule VI prescription under an applicable electronic-prescribing exception. The pharmacist receives all required information. Which statements apply to documentation of this oral order? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Reduce the oral prescription to writing with the required prescription information.
choices.why: Correct. Section 20(a) requires immediate documentation of the oral order.

choices.text: Do not impose the § 20(c) follow-up prescription requirement solely on this Schedule VI order.
choices.why: Correct. The statute expressly excludes Schedule VI substances from subsection (c).

choices.text: Dispense without creating a prescription record because the drug is Schedule VI.
choices.why: Incorrect. The Schedule VI exclusion does not eliminate the initial oral-prescription record.

choices.text: Demand a follow-up electronic prescription within two days under § 20(c) for every Schedule VI oral order.
choices.why: Incorrect. Subsection (c) does not apply to Schedule VI.

choices.text: Apply the federal emergency Schedule II seven-day documentation requirement to the Schedule VI order.
choices.why: Incorrect. That federal requirement addresses a different schedule and emergency prescribing scenario.

questions.topic: Oral order from an unfamiliar practitioner
questions.trigger: A pharmacist receives an otherwise permissible oral Schedule VI order from a practitioner the pharmacist does not know. The caller supplies a name and registration number but the pharmacist has not verified the source of the authorization. What is the pharmacist's responsibility?
questions.legal_decision: Make a reasonable effort to determine that the oral authorization came from a registered practitioner.
questions.critical_exception: The practitioner is not known to the pharmacist; the oral route is otherwise permitted.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the practitioner is already known to the pharmacist, this specific unfamiliar-practitioner verification trigger does not apply, although ordinary validity duties remain.
questions.stem: A pharmacist receives an otherwise permissible oral Schedule VI order from a practitioner the pharmacist does not know. The caller supplies a name and registration number but the pharmacist has not verified the source of the authorization. What is the pharmacist's responsibility?

choices.text: Assume the caller is registered because a registration number was spoken.
choices.why: Incorrect. The statute requires reasonable verification when the practitioner is unfamiliar.

choices.text: Reject all oral prescriptions from practitioners who are not existing pharmacy contacts.
choices.why: Incorrect. The statute calls for reasonable verification, not an automatic categorical rejection.

choices.text: Ask the patient to certify the caller's credentials in place of verification.
choices.why: Incorrect. Patient certification does not replace the pharmacist's verification responsibility.

choices.text: Check only the patient's insurance eligibility.
choices.why: Incorrect. Insurance status cannot establish the registration or identity of the prescriber.

choices.text: Make a reasonable effort to verify the source of the authorization.
choices.why: Correct. This is the explicit obligation under subsection (b).

questions.topic: Partial filling of Schedule IV prescription close to expiry
questions.trigger: A valid Schedule IV prescription for 60 tablets was issued January 5. The patient has received 20 and then 25 tablets as partial fills, with no additional authorized refills. On July 2 the patient requests the balance. Which conditions apply? Assume no other restriction prevents dispensing.
questions.legal_decision: Allow up to the remaining 15 tablets before the six-month limit; record partial fills as refills.
questions.critical_exception: Partial-fill rule for Schedule III-V; no additional authorized quantity assumed.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the balance is requested after the six-month period, the remainder cannot be dispensed under this prescription.
questions.stem: A valid Schedule IV prescription for 60 tablets was issued January 5. The patient has received 20 and then 25 tablets as partial fills, with no additional authorized refills. On July 2 the patient requests the balance. Which conditions apply? Assume no other restriction prevents dispensing.  SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Dispense another 60 tablets because each partial fill is a separate new prescription.
choices.why: Incorrect. The combined partial quantities cannot exceed the total prescribed quantity.

choices.text: Dispense no more than 15 tablets on July 2.
choices.why: Correct. The first two partial fills total 45, leaving 15 within the original quantity.

choices.text: Record each partial filling in the manner required for a refill.
choices.why: Correct. Federal law requires refill-style records for these partial fillings.

choices.text: Restart the six-month validity period on the date of the second partial fill.
choices.why: Incorrect. The limit is measured from the original issue date.

choices.text: Do not dispense the remaining quantity after the six-month limit.
choices.why: Correct. An unfilled balance does not extend the prescription's validity.

questions.topic: GHB prescription medical-need notation
questions.trigger: A pharmacist receives an otherwise valid electronic prescription for gamma-hydroxybutyric acid for a legitimate medical indication. The required medical-need notation is absent from the prescription. Assume the pharmacy is otherwise authorized to dispense the product. What is the appropriate action?
questions.legal_decision: Resolve the missing practitioner medical-need notation before dispensing.
questions.critical_exception: A GHB prescription has an additional federal notation requirement; clinical legitimacy alone is insufficient.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the practitioner includes the required medical need on the prescription and all other legal conditions are met, this specific defect is resolved.
questions.stem: A pharmacist receives an otherwise valid electronic prescription for gamma-hydroxybutyric acid for a legitimate medical indication. The required medical-need notation is absent from the prescription. Assume the pharmacy is otherwise authorized to dispense the product. What is the appropriate action?

choices.text: Dispense because the drug name automatically establishes the patient's medical need.
choices.why: Incorrect. Federal law requires an explicit notation by the practitioner.

choices.text: Add an assumed medical indication based only on the patient's age and medication history.
choices.why: Incorrect. An inferred indication is not the required practitioner notation.

choices.text: Contact the prescriber to resolve the missing medical-need notation.
choices.why: Correct. The practitioner must state the patient's medical need on the prescription.

choices.text: Treat the notation as optional for electronic prescriptions.
choices.why: Incorrect. Electronic issuance does not remove the special GHB prescription requirement.

choices.text: Require the patient rather than the practitioner to complete the missing notation.
choices.why: Incorrect. The federal provision assigns the notation to the practitioner.

questions.topic: Reusable dosage planner labeling and contamination controls
questions.trigger: A patient's authorized agent requests that medications dispensed by this pharmacy be supplied in a reusable daily dosage planner. The planner has been brought from home. Which requirements must the pharmacy address before dispensing in this format?
questions.legal_decision: Apply planner-specific space, cleaning and labeling requirements; include required label information for every medication.
questions.critical_exception: The patient or agent requests the service and the drugs were not dispensed by another pharmacy.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If a drug was previously dispensed by a different pharmacy, it cannot be placed into this reusable planner under §9.07.
questions.stem: A patient's authorized agent requests that medications dispensed by this pharmacy be supplied in a reusable daily dosage planner. The planner has been brought from home. Which requirements must the pharmacy address before dispensing in this format? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Use a designated preparation space that minimizes cross-contamination.
choices.why: Correct. The regulation requires orderly preparation space with contamination prevention.

choices.text: Apply one label showing only the patient's name, regardless of the medications.
choices.why: Incorrect. The required prescription label information must cover each medication.

choices.text: Clean and store the planner to prevent contamination.
choices.why: Correct. Planner cleaning and storage must protect both the planner and pharmacy environment.

choices.text: Label the planner with the statutory information for each medication.
choices.why: Correct. Section 9.07 incorporates the medication-by-medication labeling requirements of c. 94C, § 21.

choices.text: Permit the agent to waive all pharmacy cleaning procedures by signing a consent.
choices.why: Incorrect. A request for the service does not waive required contamination safeguards.

questions.topic: Massachusetts provisional outsourcing registration: scope
questions.trigger: A Massachusetts 503B facility has been granted a provisional outsourcing facility registration because it lacks the required recent FDA inspection. It proposes sending sterile preparations to a hospital in another state before receiving its full Massachusetts registration. What is permitted under the Massachusetts provisional registration?
questions.legal_decision: Compound sterile preparations under the provisional registration, but do not distribute or dispense until FDA inspection and full Massachusetts registration.
questions.critical_exception: Other federal and state requirements remain applicable; out-of-state shipment is not exempt.
questions.counterfactual_flip: After the FDA inspection and issuance of full Massachusetts outsourcing registration, this provisional distribution prohibition is removed.
questions.stem: A Massachusetts 503B facility has been granted a provisional outsourcing facility registration because it lacks the required recent FDA inspection. It proposes sending sterile preparations to a hospital in another state before receiving its full Massachusetts registration. What is permitted under the Massachusetts provisional registration?

choices.text: Compound, but do not distribute or dispense yet.
choices.why: Correct. The provisional authority permits sterile compounding but specifically bars distribution and dispensing until inspection and full registration.

choices.text: Ship to another state because Massachusetts limits only in-state distribution.
choices.why: Incorrect. The restriction explicitly reaches distribution and dispensing both within and outside Massachusetts.

choices.text: Distribute to hospitals if each hospital assumes responsibility for product quality.
choices.why: Incorrect. A purchaser's agreement cannot expand the provisional facility registration.

choices.text: Dispense to named patients while withholding only office-use orders.
choices.why: Incorrect. The restriction covers dispensing as well as distribution of sterile preparations.

choices.text: Treat federal 503B registration alone as conversion to full Massachusetts registration.
choices.why: Incorrect. Conversion requires the Board's action after the specified FDA inspection evidence.

questions.topic: Nonresident outsourcing applicant without recent FDA inspection
questions.trigger: A nonresident 503B outsourcing facility applies to supply Massachusetts hospitals. It holds current FDA registration and a home-state facility license, but the last FDA 503B inspection was three years ago. Which statements describe Massachusetts application requirements?
questions.legal_decision: Require FDA inspection within two years preceding application; provisional registration unavailable to nonresidents; home-state good-standing evidence if licensed.
questions.critical_exception: Nonresident facility, not an ordinary nonresident pharmacy.
questions.counterfactual_flip: An FDA inspection within the preceding two years would satisfy the inspection-timing condition; other application conditions remain.
questions.stem: A nonresident 503B outsourcing facility applies to supply Massachusetts hospitals. It holds current FDA registration and a home-state facility license, but the last FDA 503B inspection was three years ago. Which statements describe Massachusetts application requirements? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Issue a provisional Massachusetts registration because federal registration is current.
choices.why: Incorrect. The provisional option is not available to a nonresident outsourcing facility.

choices.text: Require proof of an FDA inspection within the two years immediately before the application.
choices.why: Correct. The nonresident application has this express inspection timing requirement.

choices.text: Accept home-state licensure as a substitute for the required FDA inspection.
choices.why: Incorrect. Home-state licensure is separate from the FDA inspection requirement.

choices.text: Require current FDA 503B registration evidence.
choices.why: Correct. Federal registration proof is another required application element.

choices.text: Require proof of good standing from the home-state licensing authority issued within three months.
choices.why: Correct. The facility is licensed in its home state, triggering the specific recent good-standing documentation requirement.

questions.topic: Renewal of full outsourcing registration
questions.trigger: An outsourcing facility obtained full Massachusetts registration in 2026. Its manager believes that keeping the state registration current is sufficient even if the facility's FDA 503B registration expires. Which approach meets Massachusetts renewal requirements?
questions.legal_decision: Renew by the applicable December 31 odd-year expiration and provide evidence of current FDA registration.
questions.critical_exception: Full resident or nonresident outsourcing registration, not provisional registration.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the facility provides valid current FDA registration evidence and all other required materials, that renewal-document deficiency is removed.
questions.stem: An outsourcing facility obtained full Massachusetts registration in 2026. Its manager believes that keeping the state registration current is sufficient even if the facility's FDA 503B registration expires. Which approach meets Massachusetts renewal requirements? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Renew on December 31 of every even-numbered year.
choices.why: Incorrect. Full outsourcing registrations follow odd-numbered-year expiration.

choices.text: Use the original FDA registration certificate even if it is no longer valid.
choices.why: Incorrect. The renewal application requires proof of valid current registration.

choices.text: Plan for expiration on December 31, 2027.
choices.why: Correct. The first odd-numbered year following issuance in 2026 is 2027.

choices.text: Provide evidence of current FDA 503B registration with the state renewal application.
choices.why: Correct. The federal registration evidence is expressly required.

choices.text: Automatically renew by paying the federal registration fee without filing with the Board.
choices.why: Incorrect. Federal registration does not replace the Massachusetts renewal process.

questions.topic: Hazardous and nonhazardous nonsterile compounding segregation
questions.trigger: A Massachusetts specialty-licensed pharmacy compounds both hazardous and nonhazardous nonsterile preparations. It proposes using one room with two separate hoods, alternating the activities by time of day. Which arrangement satisfies the Board policy on segregation?
questions.legal_decision: Use separate rooms and separate primary engineering controls for hazardous and nonhazardous nonsterile compounding.
questions.critical_exception: This is Massachusetts nonsterile segregation policy, not a sterile cleanroom classification question.
questions.counterfactual_flip: Moving hazardous compounding into a separate compliant containment room with a separate containment hood resolves the specified segregation defect.
questions.stem: A Massachusetts specialty-licensed pharmacy compounds both hazardous and nonhazardous nonsterile preparations. It proposes using one room with two separate hoods, alternating the activities by time of day. Which arrangement satisfies the Board policy on segregation?

choices.text: Use the same room and hood if hazardous preparations are made last.
choices.why: Incorrect. Scheduling separation does not satisfy the physical segregation rule.

choices.text: Use two hoods in the same room if no simultaneous compounding occurs.
choices.why: Incorrect. Separate hoods alone do not satisfy the required room separation.

choices.text: Use one room for all nonsterile preparations if personnel wear additional PPE.
choices.why: Incorrect. Personal protective equipment does not replace the specified engineering controls.

choices.text: Use a nonhazardous compounding area for hazardous compounding when its surfaces are cleaned afterward.
choices.why: Incorrect. Cleaning does not create the required separate containment room and hood.

choices.text: Use a separate hazardous-drug room and separate containment hood.
choices.why: Correct. The Board specifically requires both room and primary engineering control separation.

questions.topic: Scale annual sealing in simple nonsterile compounding
questions.trigger: During a November inspection, a simple nonsterile compounding pharmacy shows that its scale was sealed in December of the prior calendar year. It has not yet been sealed in the current year. The manager proposes postponing the next sealing until the following February. Which action is required?
questions.legal_decision: Arrange sealing within the current calendar year and keep equipment properly maintained.
questions.critical_exception: A scale used in nonsterile compounding; no waiver assumed.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If it has already been properly sealed during the current calendar year, the annual sealing requirement is met for that year.
questions.stem: During a November inspection, a simple nonsterile compounding pharmacy shows that its scale was sealed in December of the prior calendar year. It has not yet been sealed in the current year. The manager proposes postponing the next sealing until the following February. Which action is required?

choices.text: Arrange sealing before the current calendar year ends.
choices.why: Correct. The policy requires sealing at least once per calendar year.

choices.text: Postpone sealing until February because the prior seal remains acceptable for two years.
choices.why: Incorrect. The requirement is annual, not biennial.

choices.text: Substitute a staff member's visual inspection for the required sealing.
choices.why: Incorrect. Routine examination does not substitute for sealing.

choices.text: Require sealing every week solely because the scale is used for compounding.
choices.why: Incorrect. The cited policy sets an annual sealing requirement and proper maintenance, not weekly sealing.

choices.text: Apply the sealing rule only to pharmacies with a complex nonsterile specialty license.
choices.why: Incorrect. The equipment requirement is within the general facility and equipment section, not limited to specialty pharmacies.

questions.topic: DEA records for retail pharmacy LTCF automated dispensing systems
questions.trigger: A DEA-registered retail pharmacy operates an automated dispensing system at a long-term care facility under an additional DEA registration as required by federal law. It proposes maintaining the controlled-substance records for that system at the retail pharmacy. Which statements are correct under the federal record-location rule? Assume other applicable state and federal records duties are met.
questions.legal_decision: The additional-registration records may be kept at the retail pharmacy or an approved central location.
questions.critical_exception: This applies to a registered retail pharmacy's additional LTCF automated dispensing registration, not a general permission for all locations.
questions.counterfactual_flip: An arbitrary unapproved off-site location that is neither the retail pharmacy nor an approved central location would not satisfy this particular allowance.
questions.stem: A DEA-registered retail pharmacy operates an automated dispensing system at a long-term care facility under an additional DEA registration as required by federal law. It proposes maintaining the controlled-substance records for that system at the retail pharmacy. Which statements are correct under the federal record-location rule? Assume other applicable state and federal records duties are met. SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Keep the records for the additional LTCF registration at the retail pharmacy.
choices.why: Correct. The federal provision expressly permits this record location.

choices.text: Discard separate records for the LTCF system because the retail pharmacy has a registration.
choices.why: Incorrect. The location allowance is not a waiver of the applicable recordkeeping requirements.

choices.text: Use an approved central recordkeeping location as permitted by the regulation.
choices.why: Correct. The same provision permits an approved central location.

choices.text: Store the only records at any unaffiliated warehouse without approval.
choices.why: Incorrect. The specified alternate record locations do not include any arbitrary unapproved facility.

choices.text: Assume the records need not be available for regulatory inspection if they are kept at the retail pharmacy.
choices.why: Incorrect. Permitted record location does not remove recordkeeping and inspection obligations.
